name: BACH_0161
markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests InSitu (98%)** · Confident · Careful review
Single-class set and high reliability, but the second model disagrees [F1].

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | InSitu 98%, Invasive 2% | Strongly InSitu |
| Conformal set | InSitu only (90%) | Single class |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.97 / 62nd percentile | Typical, usable input |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | No | Different top class |
| Similar cases | 4 of 5 InSitu [F5] | Mostly supportive |

## Tissue evidence
- **Tumor cell fraction** (regions 2, 5, 9) · context · 87% neoplastic nuclei; highest in reference set [F7] · Measured
- **Atypical cells confined within ducts** (region 5) · ↓ invasive · Associated with in situ rather than invasive growth · Weak
- **Tumor infiltrating stroma** (region 11) · ↓ invasive · Near-typical score; small effect here · Validated
- **Marked nuclear pleomorphism** (region 7) · ↓ invasive · Typical score; does not push toward invasive · Validated
- **Normal lobules** (regions 7, 11) · ↓ invasive · Scored above typical; association not trustworthy [F2] · Unreliable

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing the top 3 regions drops the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful.
- **Concepts**: Concept deletion CI includes 0 (−0.005 to 0.007), so not shown faithful; normal lobules (0/20) is Unreliable.

## Could be wrong if
- The second model (MUSK) picks another top class, so the InSitu call lacks independent confirmation.
- One similar case, BACH_0138, is Invasive (similarity 89%); invasion may be under-called.

## Check on the slide
1. **Regions 2, 5, 9**: confirm tumor cells stay within ducts, without stromal infiltration.
2. **Region 11**: look for invasive nests in stroma; peak for the stromal-infiltration concept.
3. **Region 7**: check pleomorphism; also top region for the unreliable lobules concept.
